H3: On the Specificity of Selectors
P: The specificity of the :not() pseudo-class is the specificity of its argument. The :not() pseudo-class does not add to the selector specificity, unlike other pseudo-classes.
P: The simple selector that :not() takes as an argument can be any of the following:
LI: Type selector (e.g p , span , etc.)
LI: Class selector (e.g .element , .sidebar , etc.)
LI: ID selector (e.g #header )
LI: Pseudo-class selector (e.g :first-child , :last-of-type )
H3: Reference
P: The argument passed to :not() can not , however, be a pseudo- element selector (such as ::before and ::after , among others) or another negation pseudo-class selector.
